objective: Freeze the reviewed product acceptance and machine-readable architecture contracts for the We Remember MVP before any implementation worker starts

launch_guards.condition: The selected remote base ref contains the fleet control plane, AGENTS.md, and this approved planning lineage
launch_guards.unblock_evidence: A fetched remote SHA containing scripts/fleet.py, .agents/fleet.json, and AGENTS.md

launch_guards.condition: Product acceptance is reviewed by the product owner and plan_status is changed from draft to approved
launch_guards.unblock_evidence: Reviewed PRD decision record and an approved docs/product/mvp-acceptance.json

launch_guards.condition: base_ref and the first wave base are replaced with the exact reviewed remote ref
launch_guards.unblock_evidence: fleet.py validate succeeds after the replacement and git rev-parse resolves the ref

launch_guards.condition: One reviewed Fleet control-plane lineage is selected and the alternate failed Run is explicitly excluded or reconciled
launch_guards.unblock_evidence: A control decision names the requested archive checksum, selected base ref and SHA, and treatment of the failed alternate Run

launch_guards.condition: Fleet launch code enforces plan_status and launch_authorized before creating any Orca Run state
launch_guards.unblock_evidence: A targeted automation test proves draft or launch_authorized=false is rejected before Run creation

constraints: This Epoch writes product and architecture documents only; it must not add application code, dependencies, lockfiles, deployment configuration, or credentials.

The 96-hour MVP is limited to three member roles, three responsibility domains, one blocked-and-accepted handover, one deterministic care escalation chain, one responsibility report, and the explicit privacy controls in the PRD.
Private agent_dm evidence is local-first and self-visible by default; no shared write occurs without explicit speaker consent and an enforced visibility scope.
AI may draft ambiguous interpretations only. Authorization, state transitions, reminders, care escalation, deletion, export, and audit remain deterministic.
Missing information, invalid structured output, missing confirmation, or unknown safety policy produces blocked or human-confirmation state, never implicit success.
No real household, health, account, or credential data may appear in fixtures, logs, prompts, documentation, or evidence.
Visual implementation cannot start until platform, viewport matrix, states, assets, tokens, and screenshot acceptance are frozen.
Implementation checks and package-manager commands must come from the accepted architecture output; this plan does not invent them.
The alternate remote Fleet branch was built from a different archive and its exhausted pre-dispatch Run is not a valid base or success receipt for this plan.

In the requested kit, plan_status and launch_authorized are review metadata only; the unresolved base ref is the current machine-enforced launch block and must remain unresolved until LG-005 is closed.
global_acceptance: The PRD is reviewed and every P0 item maps to an observable user outcome, a deterministic or AI owner, a data boundary, and a verification method.
A fictional demo fixture contract covers at least three responsibility domains, eight valid signals, and two discussion-only non-task messages.
Tech-Spec.md, API_CONTRACT.md, JSON Schemas, state-machine contracts, privacy threat model, and implementation-contract.json form one consistent source of truth.
The architecture output selects the smallest maintainable stack, exact repository layout, package manager, dependency policy, local commands, and track checks with documented tradeoffs.
The accepted architecture SHA contains the accepted product SHA in its history and is pushed without history rewriting.
No implementation Wave is generated or dispatched until all launch guards are closed and the foundation SHA is accepted.

risk_register.risk: The fleet kit exists only on a local bootstrap branch, so origin/main cannot create valid coordinator or worker worktrees.
risk_register.mitigation: Merge or push the reviewed control plane first, fetch it, then replace the blocked base ref with the exact remote ref.

risk_register.risk: The PRD is pending review and the visual source, platform constraints, and acceptance matrix are not frozen.
risk_register.mitigation: PROD-001 freezes scope, UI facts, demo truth boundaries, and a machine-readable acceptance manifest before architecture starts.

risk_register.risk: Consent, health visibility, deletion, and high-risk content errors could expose private data or create unsafe behavior.
risk_register.mitigation: Define explicit trust boundaries, deny-by-default transitions, deletion cascades, audit semantics, redacted model input, and high-risk routing in contracts and threat-model tests.

risk_register.risk: Unvalidated LLM output could silently create tasks, transfer responsibility, or activate care behavior.
risk_register.mitigation: Schema validation, one bounded retry, human-confirmation fallback, prompt versioning, and a hard rule that consequential execution is deterministic.

risk_register.risk: Ten P0 capabilities can exceed the 96-hour budget and dilute the ownership-transfer story.
risk_register.mitigation: Preserve the seven-step demo spine, remove P1 first, and require an explicit product decision before cutting any P0 surface.

risk_register.risk: No implementation stack or exact test commands are currently selected, so implementation task checks would be fictional.
risk_register.mitigation: ARCH-001 must produce implementation-contract.json with exact paths, commands, package manager, and check ownership before the implementation Epoch is authored.

risk_register.risk: The subject experience may be unusable for older adults even if automated UI checks pass.
risk_register.mitigation: Freeze accessibility criteria now and reserve a separate human usability receipt for one-tap reminder acknowledgement before release.
risk_register.gate: Product acceptance plus later QA evidence

risk_register.risk: Local tests, screenshots, HTTP responses, deployment configuration, and public runtime evidence can be confused with release or submission acceptance.
risk_register.mitigation: Require evidence labels for Local, Fixture, Public Runtime, Deployment, and Official Acceptance; never promote one level into another.
risk_register.gate: Foundation documentation and final release manifest

risk_register.risk: Two Fleet control-plane lineages with different archive provenance can create split-brain plans, duplicate Runs, and conflicting completion evidence.
risk_register.mitigation: Select one reviewed lineage by archive checksum and exact remote SHA, preserve the failed alternate Run as historical evidence, and never retry or dispatch across lineages.

risk_register.risk: The current Fleet scripts do not read plan_status or launch_authorized, so those fields alone do not stop launch.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep the intentionally unresolved base ref and add a pre-Run authorization check with a no-state-created regression test before publishing an executable shared base.

waves.description: Freeze what the MVP must prove to users and judges before technical design begins

tasks.title: Freeze MVP scope, demo truth boundaries, and observable acceptance
tasks.spec: Review the pending PRD and produce docs/product/mvp-acceptance.json, docs/product/demo-fixture-contract.json, and concise supporting Markdown. Map every P0 capability to the user problem it solves, observable states, privacy boundary, deterministic versus AI responsibility, failure behavior, demo evidence, and explicit non-goals. Resolve the PRD conflicts around family-group scope cuts, privacy-rights scope, the rephrase helper, per-item consent versus category grants, handover terminology, evidence visibility, and deletion versus audit retention. Freeze the target platform decision, viewport and accessibility matrix, required data states, visual source/assets/tokens requirements, seven-step demo spine, Fixture labeling, and 96-hour scope-cut rules. Do not choose implementation details or write product code.
acceptance: PRD status and decision log truthfully record reviewed, blocked, and deferred decisions
Every P0 item maps to an observable outcome, acceptance evidence, failure state, and owning future track
The seven-step demo includes explicit consent, neutral reporting, blocked handover, two-party acceptance, reminder transfer, deterministic care escalation, and the final workload reduction
Fixture data is fictional, contains no personal data, and defines at least three domains, eight valid signals, and two discussion-only non-tasks
Target platform, viewports, accessibility requirements, UI states, asset/token source, and screenshot QA criteria are explicit before visual work
One authoritative P0 matrix resolves family-group, privacy-rights, rephrase-helper, and consent-grant contradictions without a silent scope cut
Handover terminology, evidence access, audit retention, and deletion expectations each have one approved product rule before architecture begins
Fixture, Local, Public Runtime, Deployment, and Official Acceptance evidence remain visibly distinct in the product and demo contract
P1 and non-goals are separated from P0; any P0 cut requires a recorded product decision
mvp-acceptance.json and demo-fixture-contract.json parse successfully as UTF-8 JSON

waves.description: Translate accepted product behavior into machine-readable contracts and exact implementation inputs

tasks.title: Freeze architecture, API, schemas, state machines, security boundaries, and implementation checks
tasks.spec: Consume only the accepted PROD-001 SHA. Define the smallest maintainable architecture for the 96-hour MVP without implementation code. Produce Tech-Spec.md, API_CONTRACT.md, versioned JSON Schemas, consent and visibility policies, first-class five-stage Task ownership fields, handover and care state machines, deletion/export/audit semantics, LLMProvider and structured-output contracts, deterministic clock and demo-mode behavior, observability and redaction rules, trust-boundary threat analysis, and representative success/failure examples. Produce docs/architecture/implementation-contract.json as the sole input for the next planning Epoch; it must select the stack, package manager, repository layout, exact per-track commands, dependency policy, local run procedure, and release evidence levels with reasons and user impact.
acceptance: Task.discoveredBy, deadlineKeptBy, scheduledBy, executedBy, and followedUpBy are required persisted contract fields
agent_dm evidence remains self-visible and cannot enter shared storage without explicit speaker consent and visibility enforcement
Handover cannot enter accepted until required information and both confirmations exist; reminders move only after acceptance
Care rules require human activation and every consequential care transition is deterministic and testable with a controllable clock
Invalid or timed-out AI output gets one bounded retry and then a human-confirmation state; it cannot activate consequential behavior
Evidence deletion, consent withdrawal, AI disablement, export, and space deletion have explicit authorization, cascade, audit, and failure semantics
Conversation, Message, ConsentDecision or ShareGrant, Reminder, Handover, CareEvent, and Visibility contracts reconcile every accepted P0 interaction and state
Evidence.rawRef access and deletion, Handover retention, AuditLog retention, and space deletion are mutually consistent and testable
High-risk content routes to non-diagnostic safety guidance and never becomes an ordinary task
The selected stack and every dependency are justified against delivery speed, privacy, maintainability, and offline demo reliability
implementation-contract.json defines non-overlapping physical paths and exact build, type, lint, unit, contract, E2E, accessibility, and security checks for the next Epoch
All contract and schema JSON files parse successfully and representative success/failure examples are present
checks: python -c "import json, pathlib; files=list(pathlib.Path('contracts').rglob('*.json'))+list(pathlib.Path('schemas').rglob('*.json')); assert files, 'no contract JSON files'; [json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')) for path in files]; print(f'validated {len(files)} contract JSON files')"
